newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: AUSTRALIA YIELD SPREADS-BLOW OUT VERSUS THE BLOC.
newsitem.headline: AUSTRALIA YIELD SPREADS-BLOW OUT VERSUS THE BLOC.

text.p: Australian bonds underperformed against the dollar bloc as a U.S. inspired sell-off soured the domestic technical outlook, prompting selling by U.S. hedge funds in afternoon trading.

Until the last two trading days the local market had held up reasonably well against a steady rise in U.S. Treasury yields based on Australia's superior fundamentals, although some analysts feel that all the positive news is now priced in.

"The U.S. has been the major driver. The spread against the U.S. is still extremely low, so the optimisim on inflation and the pessimism on growth is in that spread," said Rory Robertson, fixed income analyst as Bankers Trust Australia.
"We think the domestic environment is going to be less positive over the coming six months that it has been in the past six months," he added.
The Australian 10-year bond yield spread has grown rapidly since Thursday's close to stand close to 50 basis points and some 25 basis points above the low seen last week.

The largest spread move on the day was against Canadian debt, which had outperformed the U.S. on Friday, while New Zeland bonds yields drifted down slightly as the N.Z. dollar made a minor recovery against the U.S. dollar.
